A Q4 guide in the low $100m's, or a gross margin guide below 59%, is what it falls on.

next_guide.street_next_quarter: Q4 FY27 revenue about $112.6m, derived from Yahoo's next-quarter growth estimate of 11.65% on $100.87m a year earlier (search snippet of https://sg.finance.yahoo.com/quote/AMBA/analysis/; the page returned 503, snapshot date unclear)
next_guide.street_full_year: FY27 revenue about $441m (+12.89% y/y, same Yahoo snippet). Q1 + Q2 + the Q3 midpoint = $328.0m, so $441m implies Q4 of about $113m
next_guide.company_current_guide: Q4: none. Full year: 10-15% growth on FY26 revenue of $390m, i.e. $429-449m, given in March 2026 (https://finance.yahoo.com/news/ambarella-reaffirms-fy2027-growth-edge-011831748.html), which with $328.0m through Q3 implies Q4 of $101-121m. On 2026-09-03 the CEO said the full year is 'still a little uncertain' because of memory and that Q4 should follow 'regular seasonality' barring memory impact (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262150875-tradingkey).
next_guide.basis: Regular seasonality (Q4 FY26 / Q3 FY26 = $100.9m / $108.5m, about -7%) on a $119.5m Q3 gives about $111m, close to the street, but management said in September that it was still checking whether customers could secure memory for Q4. Since then a camera peer reported memory price rises of 70-80% in late September (GoPro 10-Q), Himax guided Q4 down 22-26% on Chinese auto destocking, and Arlo's channel inventory rose to 14.9 weeks. Insta360 and Hanwha Vision growth point the other way, so the guide is likely at or below the street, not clearly a cut.

findings.finding: On the 2026-09-03 call management said Q4 FY27 (Jan quarter) should follow 'regular seasonality' only 'barring any memory impact', that it was still checking with customers whether they could secure enough memory for Q4, and that the 10-15% FY27 growth target was 'still a little uncertain'. With $328.0m booked through the Q3 midpoint, that target implies Q4 of $101-121m against a street of about $112.6m (~-6% q/q), so a memory-hit Q4 guide would land below the street.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This name trades on the guide: Q3 FY26 (Nov 2025) fell 18.78% on a lower gross margin guide despite a beat; Q1 FY27 (May 2026) fell 21.41% on a cautious outlook with memory-inflation worries; Q2 FY27 with an in-line Q3 guide moved -0.77% (baseline and https://www.earningswhispers.com/epsdetails/AMBA).
findings.why_not_priced: The memory caveat is public, and the 27.5% 20-day fall at a 52-week low prices a good part of it. What is not priced is the size: the street's ~$112.6m Q4 still assumes normal seasonality, and an implied FY27 of ~$441m sits at the top half of a 10-15% range management called uncertain. If the market had fully priced a memory cut, the Q4 and FY estimates would have come down toward $105m and $433m, and they have not visibly moved.
findings.independence: The company's own words; corroborated in direction by peer and counterparty evidence filed separately (GoPro 10-Q memory price spike, Himax Q4 guide), which are different documents. The FY27 10-15% frame comes from https://finance.yahoo.com/news/ambarella-reaffirms-fy2027-growth-edge-011831748.html (2026-03-11).

findings.finding: Earnings Whispers' 2026-11-16 preview reports days of inventory at 157 against 76 a year earlier, free cash flow negative in each of the last two quarters (IP licence payments and an inventory build), Q2 non-GAAP gross margin 59.3% below its guide midpoint after 59.9% the quarter before and 60.9% a year earlier, and says gross margin is 'the first place the bull case could crack'. The Q3 gross margin guide is 59-60%, at the bottom of the 59-62% long-term target.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Nov 2025 print fell 18.78% on a lower gross margin guide after a revenue beat (https://www.fool.com/investing/2025/11/26/why-ambarella-stock-just-crashed).
findings.why_not_priced: Published and widely read, so mostly priced. What remains is whether the Q4 gross margin guide drops below 59% on mix or cost pass-through lag. Management said memory prices do not touch its own gross margin (it does not buy memory), which caps the risk.
findings.independence: Inventory days (157 against 145 the quarter before) also come from the CFO's Q2 remarks summarised at https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262150875-tradingkey (same underlying company disclosure, so not independent).

findings.finding: Inventory days rose from 145 to 157 in Q2 FY27, while inventory dollars fell 4% q/q and DSO fell from 35 to 32. Cash fell from $277.8m to $272.3m. Inventory built ahead of 'multiple new product cycles' raises the risk of a cautious inventory or revenue tone if customer builds slip on memory.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No print in the baseline turned visibly on inventory alone.
findings.why_not_priced: Public for three months; small residual. If priced, the stock would not react to an inventory number in line with Q2's.
findings.independence: Shares the Q2 disclosure with the gross margin finding; counted once here, on the inventory line only.

findings.finding: GoPro's Q3 2026 10-Q says memory component costs rose sharply, including unexpected price increases of 70-80% in the last week of September 2026, and that it may not be able to offset them. GoPro's Q3 hardware revenue fell 49.5% and it gave no guidance. This is evidence that consumer camera OEMs, Ambarella's end market, were hit by a memory squeeze inside Ambarella's Q3 and going into its Q4.
findings.link: Same end product (action cameras, Ambarella's legacy IoT market). GoPro designs its own GP-series SoC, so it is not established as a current Ambarella customer; the link is the shared memory input and end market, not shared revenue.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 FY27 fell 21.41% when a downgrade cited memory inflation in the tech supply chain (https://www.tikr.com/blog/ambarella-fell-21-today-heres-how-much-the-stock-could-rise-in-2026).
findings.why_not_priced: It is in a 10-Q footnote of a company with no call and a pending merger, so it was barely covered; the 70-80% late-September step is dated after Ambarella last spoke (09-03) and its Citi appearance (09-17). It is a proxy, so it is small.
findings.independence: Insta360's Q3 report also cites memory price rises squeezing profit (https://wap.eastmoney.com/a/202610273910539824.html), but its revenue still grew 33%, which cuts the other way on volume.

findings.finding: Himax guided Q4 2026 revenue down 22-26% q/q on 2026-11-05, citing abrupt short-term order cuts and destocking by automotive customers, particularly Chinese automakers. Ambarella's automotive segment (about 22-25% of revenue, a record in Q2 FY27) sells ADAS and camera SoCs into the same Chinese and global auto supply chains.
findings.link: Both supply ICs to Chinese automakers' builds, but Himax sells display drivers (TDDI/DDIC), not perception SoCs. No shared named customer; auto is about a quarter of Ambarella's revenue, so the effect is net of the ~75% IoT side.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Auto has been the growth line management highlights; no print in the baseline turned on auto alone.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a different company's segment, and Himax called auto 'relatively insulated from memory'; Ambarella's auto has run at records, so analysts are unlikely to have cut Ambarella's Q4 auto on a display-driver peer. Sized small as a segment proxy, net of IoT.

findings.finding: Insta360 (Arashi Vision, 688775.SH), whose cameras use Ambarella AI SoCs (cited in the ITC Insta360 case coverage), reported Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep) revenue of RMB 3.919bn, up 33.3% y/y, with 9-month revenue up 42.7%, and said it increased inventory stocking (加大备货). Profit was squeezed by memory price rises. This overlaps two thirds of Ambarella's Aug-Oct quarter and supports IoT revenue at or above the guide midpoint.
findings.link: Insta360 360/action cameras use Ambarella AI SoCs (https://marketchameleon.com/PressReleases/i/2260942/AMBA/investor-alert-pomerantz-law-firm-investigates-claims, on the Feb 2026 ITC ruling); Insta360's share of Ambarella revenue is not disclosed (WT Microelectronics, the logistics partner, was 60.2% of Q2 revenue).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Ambarella prints revenue at its guide midpoint (Q1 FY27 $100.4m against $100.2m consensus, Q2 $108.1m against $108.03m); in-line revenue has not moved the stock up.
findings.why_not_priced: A Shanghai STAR-market filing in Chinese, released after Ambarella last spoke; US coverage did not pick it up. It lands inside the guided Q3 range, so it supports a midpoint print more than a beat, which is why it is small. The growth slowed from +50% in H1 to +33%, and the stocking may pull Q4 demand forward.
findings.independence: Hanwha Vision's record security quarter (separate finding, separate document) points the same way for IoT.

findings.finding: Hanwha Vision reported Q3 2026 (Jul-Sep) security and AI-camera revenue up 28.5% y/y, a second straight record quarter, with operating profit up 79.9%, helped by higher product prices; Hanwha signed a 10-plus-year sourcing and co-development agreement with Ambarella valued at over $800m of potential revenue on 2026-05-28.
findings.link: Hanwha is a contracted Ambarella partner (https://finviz.com/news/357946/hanwha-and-ambarella-enter-into-long-term-edge-ai-agreement), but it keeps its own Wisenet SoC in-house, so the share of its cameras on Ambarella silicon, and its current revenue to Ambarella, are not disclosed and are likely small.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Security IoT is the core of Ambarella's revenue; in-line IoT quarters have not lifted the stock (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: A Korean filing read through Korean press; it supports professional security-camera demand despite memory costs. It lands inside the guided range.
findings.independence: Insta360 finding (different end market, consumer cameras).

findings.finding: Axon reported Q3 2026 on 2026-11-05: Connected Devices +16%, personal sensors (Axon Body 4) +6.4%, margins squeezed by higher memory costs, and about $225m of 2026 cash consumed by inventory investment; it guided Q4 revenue to $990m-1.01bn. A body-camera OEM building inventory despite memory costs is mildly supportive of camera SoC demand.
findings.link: Axon body cameras are reported in trade coverage to use Ambarella SoCs; not confirmed in either company's filings, so treat it as a weak link.
findings.why_not_priced: Small, unconfirmed link; filed for breadth.
findings.independence: Zacks summary of memory-cost margin pressure: https://zacks.com/stock/news/3025433/axon-enterprise-q3-earnings-miss-estimates-as-margins-narrow

findings.finding: Arlo's Q3 2026 revenue growth slowed to about 7% y/y from 21% in Q2, its US channel inventory rose to 14.9 weeks from 5.9 ahead of Q4 promotions, and management flagged memory cost increases; it guided Q4 revenue to $137-147m. The stock fell about 8%. This signals consumer home-security camera demand cooling and channel stuffed into Ambarella's Q4.
findings.link: Same end market (consumer security cameras); Arlo's SoC supplier mix is not disclosed in what I found, so link none stated beyond the end market.
findings.source_date: 2026-11 (Earnings Whispers via Finviz, page id 418098, published around Arlo's early-November report)
findings.why_not_priced: Peer evidence that analysts rarely carry into Ambarella's model; small and unlinked.

findings.finding: The stock went into the print down 27.5% over 20 days and about 19% since the $60.12 close of 2026-11-13, sitting on its 52-week low (~$48.30-48.65, last set 2026-03-30) and about 45% below a mean target of $87.55-91.33. The fall follows the 2026-11-05 semiconductor crash (SOX -12.25% in a day) and a shift in Earnings Whispers sentiment to moderately bearish. A guide merely near the street would clear a bar the price has already lowered.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After the Q2 FY27 print, which came after a 5.1% pre-print dip with an in-line guide, the stock moved only -0.77%; the one up-move in seven (+16.78%, Aug 2025) came on a raised outlook. Five of the other six fell 14.9-21.4%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is what is priced, filed so the judges can weigh it: if the market expected a normal Q4 the stock would not have fallen ~19% in seven sessions to a 52-week low with no company news. The open question is whether the slide fully discounts a memory-hit guide; on this name's history it has usually fallen further on the guide anyway.

findings.finding: Positioning leans to a squeeze on relief: short interest 4.65m shares (~10.5% of shares outstanding, DTC 2.6) at the 2026-10-30 settlement, down from 5.71m on 09-15; the options market bids calls over puts (25-delta skew -5.2 vol points, put/call OI 0.23).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Short interest was higher (12.9%) into the Sep print, which moved -0.77%; no evidence of a squeeze on past prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The settlement predates the latest leg down (11-13 to 11-24), so shorts may have rebuilt; the skew is from a chain with a 52% ATM spread, so it is a weak signal. Filed as a modest offset to the negatives, not as a long thesis.
findings.independence: Baseline options block (skew, put/call OI), a different source.

findings.finding: The baseline's seven prior reactions are 6 down and 1 up, median |move| 16.78%, max 21.41%; four of the six declines (-14.9% to -21.4%) came on guidance or gross margin despite an in-line or beating quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: That is the line: Nov 2025 -18.78% on a lower GM guide; May 2026 -21.41% on cautious outlook and a downgrade; Feb 2026 -14.89%.
findings.why_not_priced: Base rate, not news; the options imply 12.7% with calls bid, so the market does not price this downside lean. Kept small because a stock at its 52-week low has less to give back than one near its highs.
findings.independence: Sealed baseline history (8-K item 2.02 times), a different source.

findings.finding: The Q3 revenue bar is tight: consensus $119.9m against a $119.5m guide midpoint, and Ambarella has printed within a fraction of consensus for two quarters ($100.4m against $100.2m, $108.1m against $108.03m). Counterparty growth (Insta360 +33%, Hanwha security +28.5%) argues for a print at or slightly above the midpoint; management said memory had little revenue impact in Q3.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In-line revenue quarters have been followed by moves set by the guide (-0.77% to -21.41%); the quarter itself has not paid.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: it is the base case. Filed so the bar is on the record; worth little on its own.

outside_window.finding: Hanwha's >$800m, 10-plus-year sourcing agreement and the CV8 2nm chip ramp (customer production targeted for the following year) are multi-year revenue drivers that no single print resolves.

rejected_candidates.detail: A Q2 item already reported on 2026-09-03; nothing about it lands in this print. Listed for the judges, sized 0.

rejected_candidates.detail: Routine plan selling already in the record; no Oct-Nov change found; adds nothing to the expectations finding.

baseline_tension: The negatives (memory-driven Q4 guide risk, peer destocking, a 6-of-7 down reaction history) agree with the name's history but cut against the options market, which bids calls (skew -5.2) after a 27.5% 20-day slide to a 52-week low with 10.5% of shares short, so p_up is held near 50 rather than at the 35-40 the guide evidence alone would give.
lessons_applied: Lesson 7 (positioning: crowded short and a call-bid skew against a negative): the Q4 guide finding shrank from -3.0 to -2.5 and p_up moved from 45 to 46.
Lesson 6 (inside the guided range is expected): Insta360 shrank from +1.0 to +0.5 and Hanwha Vision from +0.5 to +0.3, because both support a Q3 print inside the $115-124m guide.

Lessons 5 and 9 (a proxy is sized small, a segment net of the rest): the Himax auto destock read-across shrank from -1.0 to -0.7 because auto is about a quarter of revenue and Himax sells display drivers, and Arlo shrank from -0.5 to -0.4 with no stated link.

Lesson 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the expectations/run-up finding shrank from +2.0 to +1.5, because this name has kept falling on guides from lowered bars before (5 of 6 declines).

Left standing: the gross margin, inventory, GoPro memory, positioning, reaction history and consensus bar findings; abs_move_pct stays 15 (the guide is the line, lesson 8 argues against shrinking it).
